articles.title: A 6 GB GPU Runs a 26B LLM at 45 Tokens per Second. How to Test the Claim
articles.excerpt: A benchmark headline can make a graphics card you already own look like a local AI workstation. But a model that generates tokens quickly is not necessarily useful, and a model that fits in memory is…
articles.body: A benchmark headline can make a graphics card you already own look like a local AI workstation. But a model that generates tokens quickly is not necessarily useful, and a model that fits in memory is not necessarily equivalent to the original. That distinction matters after MAPLE, a new open-source project, claimed that a pruned Gemma 4 26B-A4B model can run at 45.4 tokens per second on an RTX 4050 laptop GPU with 6 GB of VRAM. The repository reports a compressed 4.75 GB model, all 30 layers in VRAM, and a comparison against 6.9 tokens per second for the original model with 16 of 30 layers offloaded. Those are the project's own measurements, not an independent replication.

articles.body: Eger Lang is now PeaScript . I started this project as an idea in my notebook. I called it Eger Lang first. But as it grew, the name didn't feel right anymore. PeaScript fits better. Small. Simple. Grows from a small seed. Many platforms. One peapod. What is PeaScript? PeaScript is my experimental open-source programming language. v0.1 is already running in the terminal: Welcome to Peascript Language v0.1 Experimental OpenSource Project PeaScript> It's simple right now, but it's real. And I'm building it in public, step by step. Why the name change? Eger Lang was confusing to pronounce and remember. PeaScript is easy, friendly, and memorable. It matches the vision: a tiny language that anyone can start with, but can grow big. Same project. Same vision. Better name. What's coming next?

articles.body: Tugport 0.1.31 can run as an MCP server over stdio: an agent starts tugport mcp as a command, and it gets 32 tools for projects, deploys, logs, env vars, domains, backups and the audit log, forwarded to your panel with the agent's own API key. I tested it on 8 November 2026 against the panel that runs most of my sites, using the key my own AI agent works with every day, and what stood out is how little that key can see: one project, with the operator role, and nothing else. What tugport mcp does MCP clients such as Claude Code and Codex either connect to a URL or start a command and talk to it over standard input and output. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. Here's why Venus Express mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this.

articles.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
articles.excerpt: By modeling how a planet without life develops its atmosphere, astronomers hope to be able to better distinguish rocky planets without life from those that are inhabited.
articles.body: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life.
